_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Aarti Industries (consolidated, ₹ crore, revenue NET of GST as in the audited P&L and Screener; the company's headline 'revenue' of ₹9,018 cr for FY26 includes ₹732 cr of GST). One reportable segment (Ind AS 108), so revenue grows at a single rate and the EBITDA margin is a driver; energy / non-energy and value-chain volumes are tracked as KPIs. Net debt company: treasury yield is nil, interest is an explicit line. Valued on Sep-28E EV/EBITDA (primary), with P/E and DCF cross-checks.
_revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 net revenue +43% YoY, 'primarily driven by higher input prices passed on to customers' after the West Asia conflict lifted benzene, aniline, sulphur and methanol prices; volumes fell 12% QoQ. CRISIL (29-Sep-2026) expects >15% growth in FY27; PL 9,878 cr (+19%), ICICI Direct 9,688 cr (+17%). We use +18%: full-year fuel-additive capacity of 360 kT (vs 238 kT produced in FY26), DCB debottlenecking, the $150 mn agro contract, partly offset by softer prices in H2 and the winter dip in fuel additives. FY28: volumes +10-12% (Zone IV blocks, MPP, PEDA, Augene supplies) but input prices assumed to ease, so revenue +8%. FY29: +10% (CRISIL medium-term range 10-15%).
_marginWhy: FY26 14.1%. Q1FY27 16.0% included ₹50-60 cr of inventory and currency gains; CRISIL puts the underlying margin at ~14%. FY27 14.3% (Q1 actual plus ~14% for Q2-Q4, with the usual winter softness in fuel additives). FY28-29 15.0-15.5% as Zone IV and the NCB chain (China's export-VAT rebate removal) add margin and cost savings of ₹150-200 cr accrue; still below management's 14-15%-margin path to ₹1,800-2,200 cr of FY28 EBITDA, which we think will be met a year late at the low end (Aarti missed its first FY24 EBITDA target by ~29% and its FY25 target by ~41%).
_capexWhy: FY27: management ₹700-800 cr (₹180 cr spent in Q1): Zone IV completion, the 15-year backward-integration project (₹200-250 cr over two years) and ~₹150 cr maintenance. FY28-29: CRISIL expects ₹200-250 cr a year; we use ₹300-350 cr because the backward-integration project spills into FY28 and Aarti's capex has repeatedly come in above early guidance (FY26: ~₹1,000 cr guided, ₹1,125 cr spent).
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹474 cr = 5.5% of average gross block (₹8,680 cr). Zone IV (~₹2,030 cr of capital work in progress at Mar-26) is capitalised during FY27; the engine adds only capex to the gross block and holds CWIP flat, so we use 6.0% on that smaller base to land depreciation at ~₹560-610 cr, in line with the CFO's FY28 bridge of ₹580-620 cr (May-2025 call).
_treasuryWhy: Aarti carries net debt (~₹4,300 cr at Mar-26), so no treasury income is modelled; interest is an explicit line.
_otherIncomeWhy: Non-operating income ₹5-20 cr a year (FY25 ₹17.5 cr, FY26 ₹4.9 cr before exceptional items) plus, from FY28, a small share of profit from the 50:50 Augene JV (equity-accounted; steady-state JV revenue guided at ₹300-400 cr).
_interestWhy: FY26 finance cost ₹340 cr included ₹64 cr of exchange losses on foreign-currency loans; interest proper was ₹254 cr. Q1FY27 ₹83 cr as working-capital debt rose with input prices. FY27 ₹330 cr; FY28-29 lower as capex falls and debt is repaid (scheduled repayments ₹248-350 cr a year per CRISIL). CFO's FY28 bridge assumed ~₹250-270 cr at ₹1,800 cr EBITDA; we keep more debt because our EBITDA is lower.
_taxWhy: FY26 effective tax was −15% (tax credit: income-tax depreciation on new capacity, MAT credit and deferred tax assets on tax losses). Q1FY27 14%. Management guides 10-15% for FY27 and 9-15% thereafter while Zone IV tax depreciation lasts. We use 14% / 15% / 18%: the DCF applies the FY29 rate to all later years, so we lift FY29 towards the normal ~25% rate.
_payoutWhy: DPS ₹1 in FY24-FY26 (~9% of FY26 EPS); no change expected while net debt is above the company's 2.5x target.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts free cash flow at one rate (cost of equity = WACC). Aarti has debt, so we enter a WACC: cost of equity ~13.1% (beta 1.1) weighted ~78%, post-tax cost of debt ~6.5% weighted ~22% (net debt ~₹4,300 cr vs market value ~₹17,300 cr) = ~11.6%, which is what beta 0.85 produces. The same rate rolls the value forward 6 months.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian specialty-chemical demand grows with nominal GDP; 5.5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% (FY29E) to 8% by year 15: volumes from new chemistry and fuel additives, little pricing power.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades to 5% of revenue, above maintenance, because Aarti has historically reinvested heavily; depreciation 4.5% of revenue.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Zone IV ramps on time from FY28, fuel additives run at full 360 kT with the Middle East reopening, and China's anti-involution keeps NCB margins firm: FY28 EBITDA reaches ~₹1,800 cr, the low end of guidance.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Crude-linked input prices fall and reverse the Q1 inventory gains, gasoline-naphtha cracks collapse (fuel-additive demand falls), Zone IV slips again and Chinese pricing pressure returns: EBITDA stays near ₹1,200-1,300 cr and net debt does not fall.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: The street is split between EV/EBITDA (ICICI Direct 14x FY28E) and P/E (PL 28x FY28E). We use EV/EBITDA because net debt is 3.6x EBITDA, the tax rate is temporarily 10-15% and depreciation on not-yet-earning assets depresses EPS: EBITDA less net debt captures all three. 12x = the stock's ~16x one-year-forward median since Apr-2023, less the ~31% sector de-rating (peer median vs post-2023 medians), plus ~1x for faster EBITDA growth as new capacity ramps up; no premium while ROCE (~7%) is below the cost of capital.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: The other half of the street (PL 28x FY28E EPS). 25x on Sep-28E: the stock's ~32x forward P/E median since Apr-2025 less part of the sector de-rating; lower than PL's 28x because our EPS is a year further out and taxed at only 15-18%.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at ~11.6% WACC, terminal growth 5.5%, less net debt.
